tests.title: Souls store bootstrap and live soul-update subscription coverage
tests.description: Existing store-level coverage proves relay-backed load of souls/templates, deterministic ordering, and live soul update insertion/update behavior. Difficulty: none; already present.
preconditions: Mock relay query/subscription helpers are available.
Soul/template fixtures are deterministic.
steps: Load souls and templates through the store.
Deliver live `31951` events for existing and new souls.
Inspect store ordering and update semantics.
tests.expected_result: Store bootstrap uses relay-backed data and live soul events update the visible collection without reload.
data_requirements: Stable `31951` and `31950` fixtures with deterministic timestamps.
determinism_notes: Pure store unit coverage; no network dependency.

tests.title: Souls gallery browser bootstrap and live-update journey
tests.description: New browser-level test should prove the actual `/souls` page renders relay-backed souls/templates and reflects a live update, not just store state in isolation. Difficulty: medium.
preconditions: Playwright relay/WebSocket harness can inject initial soul/template events and a follow-up live `31951` event.
steps: Open `/souls` against deterministic relay mocks.
Assert initial gallery content from bootstrap data.
Inject a live update and verify the UI refreshes accordingly.
tests.expected_result: The page shows relay-backed soul data on load and changes in response to a live soul event.
mocks: mock WebSocket relay responses including EOSE and live EVENT frames
data_requirements: At least one template and two soul records with stable ids and timestamps.
determinism_notes: Avoid sleeps; drive UI updates from explicit mocked relay events.

tests.title: Browser provisioning request signing, tag shaping, and zero-accept rejection
tests.description: Existing smoke coverage proves NIP-07 gating, provisioning request tag capture, step navigation, and explicit relay-rejection handling. Difficulty: none; already present.
preconditions: Mock NIP-07 signer and relay WebSocket harness are installed.
steps: Open `/souls/new` with and without signer availability.
Submit a valid provisioning request.
Repeat with rejecting relay responses.
tests.expected_result: Valid requests are signed with required tags; missing signer blocks submit; rejecting relays surface a publish failure and do not report success.
data_requirements: Stable agent name/id/brief/tier inputs for the wizard flow.
determinism_notes: Current spec uses `waitForTimeout`; future cleanup can reduce timing dependence but the test already exercises the intended path.

tests.title: Reactor publishes correlated 7950 errors for unauthorized and malformed 5950 requests
tests.description: New in-process reactor test should inject signed provisioning requests and capture published error events for unauthorized and malformed inputs. Difficulty: medium.
preconditions: A reactor can be built with fake signer/generator and capture publisher.
Authorized and unauthorized request pubkeys are deterministic.
steps: Deliver an unauthorized provisioning request.
Deliver malformed requests missing `agent-id` and missing brief/template/draft source.
Inspect the captured result events.
tests.expected_result: Each rejected request yields a correlated `7950` error event with `e` and `p` reply tags and no successful soul publication.
data_requirements: Stable signed `5950` event fixtures for valid and invalid shapes.
determinism_notes: No live relays; inject events directly and assert captured publish payloads.

tests.title: Full provisioner success path records eight stages and emits correlated progress and terminal success
tests.description: New integration suite should drive a successful `FullProvisioner` run with deterministic fakes and assert eight-step accounting plus correlated `6950` and `7950` behavior through the reactor. Difficulty: high.
preconditions: Fake generator, signer, publisher, and optional adapters are available.
A non-placeholder provisioning engine is wired into the reactor.
steps: Execute a successful provisioning request through the reactor/full provisioner.
Capture progress and terminal result events.
Inspect run step ordering and completion state.
tests.expected_result: The run records the documented eight stages, emits meaningful progress, and concludes with correlated terminal success rather than implicit completion.
data_requirements: Stable brief, agent id, allowed kinds, tool grants, and deterministic ids/timestamps where assertions depend on ordering.
determinism_notes: Freeze or normalize timestamps/UUIDs where asserted; avoid external service calls entirely.

tests.title: Unconfigured optional integrations are recorded as skipped without fake outputs
tests.description: Existing hardening coverage proves optional avatar/Qdrant/memory/workspace steps are skipped and do not populate fake outputs when unconfigured. Difficulty: none; already present.
preconditions: FullProvisioner is constructed without optional adapter configuration.
steps: Run provisioning with optional integrations absent.
Inspect final soul outputs and recorded step statuses.
tests.expected_result: Skipped steps are explicit and optional outputs remain empty.
data_requirements: Stable provisioning request fixture with standard tier.
determinism_notes: Pure in-process coverage; no external services involved.

tests.title: Optional integration failures are surfaced as failed steps without fabricated success
tests.description: Extend provisioner coverage with deterministic optional-adapter failures so the matrix proves non-fatal failure accounting, not just skipped-path behavior. Difficulty: medium.
preconditions: At least one optional adapter can be replaced with a deterministic failing fake.
steps: Run provisioning with avatar, Qdrant, memory, or workspace adapters configured to fail non-fatally.
Inspect step results and final soul outputs.
tests.expected_result: The failed optional step is recorded as failed, downstream provisioning continues where intended, and absent outputs are not fabricated.
mocks: capture publisher if progress assertions are included
data_requirements: Stable optional-step failure messages for assertions.
determinism_notes: Use fakes that fail immediately and predictably.

tests.title: Successful provisioning publishes authoritative 31951 metadata and correlated 7950 success payload
tests.description: New contract test should capture the published `31951` soul event and the terminal `7950` success payload after successful provisioning. Difficulty: medium.
preconditions: A successful provisioning run can be executed in-process with a capture publisher.
steps: Execute successful provisioning through the reactor.
Capture the published `31951` event and terminal result event.
Inspect required tags and payload fields.
tests.expected_result: `31951` carries authoritative soul metadata and the terminal result references the published soul through correlated success data.
data_requirements: Stable agent id, npub/pubkey, and metadata fixtures.
determinism_notes: Assert on structured tags/content rather than exact ids when ids are generated dynamically.

tests.title: Browser can discover a freshly provisioned soul from relay-backed publication
tests.description: New browser journey should bridge successful provisioning to subsequent relay-backed soul discovery in the UI. Difficulty: high.
preconditions: Playwright harness can inject a provisioning success result and a follow-up `31951` publication.
steps: Complete a mocked successful provisioning flow.
Navigate to or refresh the Souls gallery.
Deliver or expose the resulting `31951` event and inspect UI visibility.
tests.expected_result: The newly provisioned soul appears through normal relay-backed browsing rather than an out-of-band UI shortcut.
data_requirements: Consistent request id, soul coordinate, and display metadata across provisioning and gallery assertions.
determinism_notes: Drive post-provision visibility from explicit mocked relay events, not sleeps.

tests.title: Bahia integration registers the provisioned soul as a service, attempts initial deployment hookup, and syncs deploy status
tests.description: New Bahia integration suite should verify service registration, initial deployment-hookup behavior, and deploy-status mapping for a provisioned soul. Difficulty: high.
preconditions: A fake or in-memory RegistryService can record created services, intents, observations, and environment state.
BahiaIntegration is configured with an agent environment id.
steps: Register a provisioned soul as a service.
Invoke initial deployment hookup.
Simulate environment state and latest observation lookups for deploy-status sync.
tests.expected_result: Service registration succeeds, deployment hookup behavior is exercised for the configured environment, and sync returns publishable deploy-status values.
data_requirements: Stable service/environment UUIDs and representative drift/health states.
determinism_notes: Use in-memory registry fakes; do not rely on real runtime adapters or databases.

tests.title: Browser lifecycle action publisher signs and correlates 1950 action events
tests.description: Existing unit coverage proves `publishSoulAction` and `updateSoulDetails` emit signed `1950` action events with soul/action/reason correlation tags. Difficulty: none; already present.
preconditions: Authenticated browser-store auth mock and Nostr publish mock are available.
steps: Publish a lifecycle action from the store.
Publish a regenerate/update action with JSON payload.
Inspect the signed event shape.
tests.expected_result: The store signs and publishes correlated `1950` action events with the expected soul coordinate and action metadata.
data_requirements: Stable soul coordinate and reason/brief payloads.
determinism_notes: Pure store unit coverage; no relay dependency.

tests.title: Lifecycle handler rejects malformed or unauthorized actions and processes valid correlated actions
tests.description: New lifecycle-handler suite should prove malformed/unauthorized rejection and valid action processing against an existing soul. Difficulty: medium.
preconditions: LifecycleHandler can be built with fake reactor, signer, and optional Bahia integration/status sync fakes.
steps: Deliver malformed action events missing soul or action tags.
Deliver unauthorized action events.
Deliver valid signed suspend/resume/regenerate/redeploy actions.
tests.expected_result: Malformed and unauthorized actions fail without state mutation; valid actions are processed against the target soul and publish correlated updates/results.
data_requirements: Stable action events with predictable soul coordinates and auth identities.
determinism_notes: Use injected fakes for GetSoul and publish capture rather than live relay queries.

tests.title: Managed lifecycle actions propagate deployment/runtime side effects for Bahia-managed souls
tests.description: New lifecycle/Bahia integration coverage should verify suspend, resume, revoke, and redeploy perform managed side effects instead of only republishing soul state. Difficulty: high.
preconditions: A Bahia-managed soul fixture exists with service id.
Bahia integration and signer side-effect collaborators can be observed deterministically.
steps: Execute suspend, resume, revoke, and redeploy actions against the managed soul.
Inspect downstream integration calls and resulting soul/action state.
tests.expected_result: Each lifecycle action triggers the corresponding managed side effect plus the expected soul/action result signaling.
data_requirements: Stable service UUID and lifecycle action fixtures.
determinism_notes: Record side-effect calls directly in fakes; avoid live runtime dependencies.

tests.title: Regenerate requires a new brief and republishes updated soul identity content
tests.description: New regenerate-specific handler coverage should prove missing-brief failure and successful republish of updated soul content plus correlated action result. Difficulty: medium.
preconditions: LifecycleHandler is configured with fake generator, signer, and publish capture.
steps: Execute regenerate without a new brief.
Execute regenerate with a valid new brief.
Inspect updated soul publication and action result.
tests.expected_result: Missing-brief regenerate fails; valid regenerate repopulates soul identity content and publishes a correlated completion result.
fixtures: fake generator with deterministic regenerated content
data_requirements: Stable original and replacement briefs with expected generated outputs.
determinism_notes: Keep generator output deterministic so republished content can be asserted exactly.

tests.title: CLI Soul Factory commands perform real Nostr-backed query and mutation flows
tests.description: Current CLI tests prove unavailability stubs. They must be replaced or extended to assert real list/get/provision/lifecycle/template behavior once transport is implemented. Difficulty: high.
preconditions: CLI signing/auth and relay query/publish support exist.
Deterministic relay fixtures or an in-process relay harness are available.
steps: Run each Soul Factory CLI command against deterministic fixtures.
Inspect query output, publish behavior, and surfaced correlated failures.
tests.expected_result: CLI commands perform real query or signed publish work instead of returning explicit unavailability errors.
data_requirements: Stable command-line args and output fixtures for list/get/provision/lifecycle/template commands.
determinism_notes: Keep CLI tests in-process or against a fully deterministic relay harness; no live relays.

tests.title: MCP Soul Factory tools perform real query, mutation, and status flows
tests.description: Current MCP-related coverage proves unavailability for list/template and only partial get/status behavior. A real MCP suite is needed once signed publish/query support exists. Difficulty: high.
preconditions: MCP server can be configured with real or fake signed Nostr publish/query capabilities and run state capture.
steps: Invoke list/get/template/provision/action/regenerate/status tools.
Inspect whether each tool performs real work and returns real query or run-status data.
tests.expected_result: The MCP surface performs real Soul Factory operations instead of returning static unavailability errors.
fixtures: MCP request fixtures for each tool
mocks: fake signer and query/publish transport where needed
data_requirements: Stable tool argument fixtures and predictable run ids/results.
determinism_notes: Status assertions should use deterministic in-memory run state, not external polling.

tests.title: Provisioning tracker no longer treats timeout or relay closure alone as normative terminal failure
tests.description: Existing store tests currently assert the opposite contract: they expect terminal failure on local timeout and relay closure. Those tests must be rewritten to encode the approved event-driven semantics. Difficulty: medium.
preconditions: Store-level provisioning tracker can be exercised with fake timers and mocked relay callbacks.
steps: Start a provisioning run without terminal result events.
Advance time and close the subscription before a correlated terminal result arrives.
Exercise explicit publish rejection and explicit correlated terminal error cases.
tests.expected_result: Local time passage and closure alone are non-terminal; only explicit rejection or correlated terminal results conclude the run.
data_requirements: Stable request ids and deterministic result payloads/errors.
determinism_notes: The current timeout/closure tests should be inverted or removed once replacement behavior exists.

tests.title: Status sync republishes deploy-status from Bahia events without relying on ticker polling
tests.description: New status-sync coverage should prove deployment-intent and deployment-run events can update soul deploy status and republish soul state, while the approved contract does not depend on `StartPeriodicSync`. Difficulty: medium.
preconditions: StatusSyncHandler can be built with fake reactor signer/publisher and fake Bahia events.
steps: Register a Bahia-managed soul.
Deliver deployment-intent-created and deployment-run-completed events.
Inspect republished soul state and deploy-status transitions.
tests.expected_result: Deploy-status updates are driven by explicit events and republished into soul state without requiring ticker-based refresh as the normative mechanism.
mocks: Bahia event payloads and service-id lookup inputs
data_requirements: Stable service UUID, event types, drift/health status fixtures.
determinism_notes: Do not use sleeps or tickers in the test; inject event callbacks directly.

known_gaps: No reactor-level provisioning request/result suite currently exists for unauthorized, malformed, or successful provisioning paths.
No backend suite currently proves authoritative `31951` publication, Bahia initial deployment hookup, or lifecycle propagation side effects.
Existing browser-store tests still encode timeout and relay-closure terminal failure semantics that now contradict approved AC-013.
Current CLI and MCP tests prove fail-closed stubs rather than the approved real transport/query behavior.
No browser E2E currently proves a freshly provisioned soul becomes visible in the relay-backed Souls gallery.

implementation_notes: Difficulty estimate — low/no new work: SFTP-T-001, SFTP-T-003, SFTP-T-006, and SFTP-T-011 already exist and should be reused as supporting evidence.
Difficulty estimate — medium: SFTP-T-004, SFTP-T-007, SFTP-T-008, SFTP-T-012, SFTP-T-014, SFTP-T-017, and SFTP-T-018 are in-process unit/integration additions with deterministic fakes.
Difficulty estimate — high: SFTP-T-002, SFTP-T-005, SFTP-T-009, SFTP-T-010, SFTP-T-013, SFTP-T-015, and SFTP-T-016 depend on broader missing implementation or multi-surface harnessing.

Recommended sequence: first add backend in-process tests for reactor/provisioner/lifecycle/status-sync semantics, then add Bahia integration coverage, then update browser tests, and only after implementation matures replace the CLI/MCP stub tests.

Use deterministic helpers throughout: fake signer, fake generator, capture publisher, fixed UUID/time fixtures where assertions depend on ordering, and mocked relay EVENT/EOSE/OK frames rather than live relays or sleeps.
